newsitem.title: USA: Anadarko sees Q2 earnings below views - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Anadarko sees Q2 earnings below views - WSJ.

text.p: Anadarko Petroleum Corp Chairman Robert Allison told the Wall Street Journal that the company will report second quarter earnings below analysts' estimates of $0.29 per share and that the company made a potentially significant oil find in Algeria.
Last year the company reported earnings of $0.30 per share in the second quarter.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the Journal says Allison predicted the company will report full year earnings very close to the First Call consensus of $1.63 a share.
Allison said oil and natural gas prices were about 10 percent lower in the quarter than in the year-earlier quarter.
Separately, Allison is quoted as saying Anadarko made a potentially significant oil discovery in Algeria that may indicate that one of the country's major oil fields is larger than had been thought.
The story says Allison believes the discovery could be an extension of the giant Qoubba field.
"It looks like there could be very significant reserves," the Journal quotes Allison as saying.
The article says Anadarko's new well, drilled in its concession five miles north of the field, is flowing high-quality oil at more than 1,200 barrels a day.
Allison said the properties of the oil are identical to that found in Qoubba, which the company discovered in 1994, according to the article.
